assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a genuinely new class of quantum states of matter, characterized by topology rather than symmetry breaking, with protected edge states and a rich follow-on literature in materials and devices. The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 invariant is conceptually original and clear.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele's theory (graphene-based quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 classification) and Molenkamp's HgTe/CdTe experimental observation form a natural theory-plus-experiment prize. Credit for the HgTe proposal (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang) and for three-dimensional topological insulators is outside the supplied credited names, so the allocation is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of independent confirmation across many materials (HgTe, Bi-based compounds, ARPES and transport), and the band-structure picture is well reproduced by first-principles calculations. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Proposed credit omits other decisive contributors outside the credited names, notably the HgTe theory proposal and 3D topological insulator work.
Overlap with the separately listed quantum anomalous Hall candidate means the prize scope would need careful definition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the central modern framework for strongly correlated electrons, giving a controlled non-perturbative description of the Mott transition and, combined with DFT (LDA+DMFT), a quantitative route to real correlated materials. This is close to my own field and has had large, lasting methodological impact.
assessment.attribution: Vollhardt (with Metzner) introduced the infinite-dimensional limit, and Georges and Kotliar established the mapping to a self-consistent impurity problem; this is a plausible three-person configuration. Other early contributors such as Mueller-Hartmann and Janis are not in the credited names, so some credit questions remain.
assessment.maturity: Two and a half decades of applications, benchmarking against experiment (spectroscopy, transport) and cluster extensions. It is mature, though predictive accuracy for specific materials still depends on choices of double counting and correlated subspace.
uncertainties: Quantitative predictive power for real materials is uneven, as results depend on implementation choices.
Discovery is a method and framework rather than a single observed phenomenon, which some members may weigh differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene revealed correlated insulators and superconductivity in a tunable two-dimensional platform, creating the moire quantum matter field. The surprise that a simple carbon system hosts flat bands and unconventional phases is the kind of quantum surprise I value.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018. That makes a clear theory-plus-experiment configuration. Other experimental groups (e.g., Dean, Young, Yazdani, Efetov) have strong claims on adjacent results.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly expanding and repeatedly reproduced across groups, but the superconducting mechanism remains debated and sample sensitivity is significant. Recognition is arguably still somewhat early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of the superconductivity is not settled.
Sample-to-sample variability and twist-angle disorder complicate the clean interpretation.
Credit for adjacent experimental advances is outside the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnel magnetoresistance in crystalline MgO junctions combines a first-principles spin-filtering prediction with an experimental demonstration of very large room-temperature effects, and it underpins hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It is a clear physical mechanism, coherent symmetry-selective tunnelling, with major technological use.
assessment.attribution: Butler's DFT-based prediction of coherent tunnelling, together with the 2004 experimental realisations by Parkin's and Yuasa's groups, gives a coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration. Others, such as Mathon and Umerski on theory and Djayaprawira on early experiments, are not credited here and could make allocation contested. The earlier discovery of GMR was already recognised in 2007.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and commercialised for nearly two decades, so it is mature. The risk is that the Nobel Committee may regard it as incremental after the 2007 GMR prize.
uncertainties: Possible view that this is an engineering refinement of the already-recognised GMR field.
Credit among Butler, Mathon and Umerski on theory and between several experimental groups is not fully settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on magic-wavelength trapping, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and is opening applications from relativistic geodesy to tests of fundamental constants and a prospective redefinition of the second. The invention is original and has clear, lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye led the experimental realisation of record accuracy and many-body clock physics. A two-laureate configuration is natural, though Hall and Hansch (frequency combs) were already recognised and others such as Hollberg and Diddams could be mentioned.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs have confirmed performance and the redefinition roadmap is under way. Recognition is timely; the main caveat is that the redefinition has not yet occurred.
uncertainties: Possible competition from ion clocks (Wineland-related work is already honoured) and from other clock groups.
Formal redefinition of the second has not yet happened.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides the architecture for superconducting quantum processors and exposes strong light-matter coupling in a solid-state setting. The importance is great and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits makes this a natural continuation.
assessment.attribution: Blais with Schoelkopf and collaborators proposed circuit QED, Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. The credited trio is a plausible configuration, though Devoret, Martinis and others are already Nobel laureates in this area, which complicates the narrative.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed across many groups and now technologically central. A second prize close to the 2025 award might look premature or repetitive to some members.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may argue for waiting.
Boundary between the discovery of strong coupling and later quantum-computing engineering is blurred.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise Hubbard models with tunable parameters, enabling quantitative study of the Mott transition and magnetism, which complements my interest in correlated-electron theory. The field is broad and influential, though the single discovery is less sharply defined.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch) proposed the Hubbard-model realisation; Greiner and Bloch demonstrated the superfluid-Mott transition and Esslinger realised the fermionic Mott insulator. Greiner is credited but I would favour Bloch, Esslinger and Zoller; the broad field raises allocation disputes.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and mature as a platform; recent quantum-gas microscopy has improved the quantitative tie to theory. Questions persist about whether it has answered open questions in the physics of correlated electrons.
uncertainties: Impact so far is more on method than on a decisive discovery about real materials.
Overlap with the other atomic-physics and quantum simulation candidates complicates the scope of a prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetically driven ferroelectricity and strong magnetoelectric coupling are a notable discovery in complex oxides, linking magnetism and electric polarisation through spin order, an area close to my own expertise on magnetic interactions. Electrical control of magnetism is of potential technological interest.
assessment.attribution: Cheong and Tokura made decisive contributions to the discovery and understanding of multiferroics and magnetoelectric coupling; Ramesh is better known for thin-film BiFeO3 multiferroics and room-temperature devices. I would propose a two-person configuration, but the credit among Kimura, Spaldin, Fiebig and others is plausibly contested.
assessment.maturity: The field is well established but practical device impact has remained limited, and the theory of spin-driven polarisation is still debated in some materials. Recognition could be premature in terms of impact.
uncertainties: Technological promise has not yet been realised in devices.
Several important contributors outside the credited names, including theorists and early experimenters, complicate attribution.
